references.text: Psalm 33:7 describes how God gathers the waters of the sea into a heap and stores the deeps, reflecting God's action with the waters in Gen 1:9.
A poetic description of creation where God sets boundaries for the waters so they will not cover the earth again, parallel to the gathering of the waters in Gen 1:9.
God speaks of setting doors and limits for the sea when it broke forth, which is a direct parallel to God gathering the waters and letting dry land appear.
Jeremiah describes how God set sand as an eternal boundary for the sea, so that it cannot cross it—a reference to God's ordering of the waters at creation.
Wisdom tells us that God set a limit for the sea so that the water would not overstep his command, and established the foundations of the earth.
Peter refers to how heaven and earth were formed by God's word, out of water and through water, a direct reference to the creation account in Gen 1:9.
A prophetic metaphor where God's saving act is described as a new creation, parallel to the original creation of land.
God's creative power over land in Genesis is the basis for his promise to restore and give the land to the people in prophecy.
Contrast between the order of creation (waters gathered for land) and the distortion of judgment (rain turning into dust that destroys the land).
Contrast between the order of creation (land created) and the distortion of prophecy (heaven and earth disappearing).
The act of creation (1:9) is the basis for God's sustaining care and provision over the earth in the Psalm.
Direct contrast: Creation gathers water to form land, while judgment releases the water to destroy the land.
A direct reference to creation: Revelation confirms that God is the Creator of what was created in Genesis.
